cards.text: The wall around Jerusalem is UP, friend. Nehemiah, the man who led the rebuild, is telling us what comes next in his own words. He's got one more thing to put in place.

cards.question: With Jerusalem's wall rebuilt, what does Nehemiah set in place?
With the doors hung on Jerusalem's gates, the ___ are appointed, along with the singers and the Levites.

cards.text: Next, somebody has to run Jerusalem, and Nehemiah puts his own brother Hanani in charge. Making your brother the boss takes a BRAVE man.

cards.question: Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge of Jerusalem along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress. What reason does Nehemiah give for his choice?

answers.text: He was faithful and feared God more than most
He had fought off the enemies at the wall
He knew every family living in the city

cards.text: Then Nehemiah gives Hanani and Hananiah their orders for the gates. When it comes to this city, the man is taking ZERO chances.

cards.question: Nehemiah tells them to open the gates of Jerusalem at first light, as early as they can.

cards.text: The gates stay closed until the sun is hot, so the gates of Jerusalem just got a snooze button! And while the guards are on duty, the doors stay shut and securely fastened.

cards.question: Somebody has to keep watch over Jerusalem. Who does Nehemiah want appointed as the guards?

answers.text: Soldiers sent by the king of Persia
Hired men from the nearby towns

cards.text: Now step back and take a look at Jerusalem. The city is large and spacious, all wrapped up in that rebuilt wall.

cards.question: Jerusalem is large and spacious, with ___ people living in it.
At least the houses inside Jerusalem's walls have all been rebuilt.

cards.text: Then Nehemiah says his God put something into his heart. And friend, when God puts something in your heart, you do NOT hit snooze on that.

cards.question: God puts it into Nehemiah's heart to gather the nobles, the officials and the people, so they can be enrolled by ___.

cards.text: Then Nehemiah finds something worth keeping. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with receipts nobody would ever need, so this man's got me JEALOUS.

cards.question: Right when Nehemiah wants the people enrolled by genealogy, what does he find?

answers.text: The register of those who first returned
A letter from the king of Persia
The scroll of the Law of Moses

cards.text: Here's what's in it: the people who came back to Jerusalem and Judah from captivity in Babylon, listed family by family and town by town with their counts, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers and temple servants included. Some families couldn't prove they came from Israel, and some priests couldn't find their family records, so those priests were kept out of the priesthood and told not to eat the most holy things until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim.

All told, the whole assembly is 42,360, plus servants, singers, horses, mules, camels and 6,720 donkeys, and that's not a moving day, that's a whole ZIP CODE on the road. Then the governor, some heads of families and the rest of the people give gold, silver and priestly garments to the treasury for the project.

cards.question: In the end, all the Israelites move inside Jerusalem's walls to live.

cards.text: Everybody settles in their own towns, and by the seventh month the Israelites are home. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card calls Nehemiah "the man who led the rebuild." That fact comes from outside the passage (Nehemiah 2–6), but the card cites only Nehemiah 7:1 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: In Nehemiah 7:2, the text doesn't make clear whether "he was a faithful man who feared God more than most" describes Hanani or Hananiah. In the BSB wording it most naturally follows Hananiah. Card 4 is all about Hanani, and this question asks for the reason behind Nehemiah's "choice." Together they lead the baker to read the reason as being about Hanani, or about both men. The card should keep the reason tied to the text's wording and leave open who it describes.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answer "Hired men from the nearby towns" isn't a real detail from the Bible. It's an invented group.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't land. Papa Dorin says he spent years with useless receipts, "so this man's got me JEALOUS." It isn't clear what he's jealous of, or how finding a register connects to his drawer. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The register Nehemiah finds ("I found the following written in it," 7:5) runs as one long stretch of lists, counts and gift totals from 7:6 through 7:72. The walkthrough sums it up in two story cards in a row (cards 17 and 18) instead of one.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card.
